prompt.garment: an oversized short-sleeve t-shirt in 175gsm 100% combed cotton jersey (30/1 yarn) with a stone-washed vintage finish, {COR}, boxy wide body, dropped shoulders with the seam on the upper arm, wide short sleeves ending just above the elbow, 2x1 ribbed crew neck, straight hem below the hip, completely plain with no print
prompt.bottom: off-white cotton drawstring trousers with a black drawstring hanging at the front
prompt.colors: VMG, CHU, AJN, CRJ, CST, VNN, RSN, RSC, CRE, OFF, LRN, AZC, MAR, ARY, PRT (15 cores)
prompt.behavior: Fabric and construction: light-to-medium 175gsm 100% combed cotton single jersey (30/1 yarn), cut oversized, pre-shrunk and anti-torsion, soft and lived-in. The garment is stone-washed after sewing, so the fade is irregular and every piece looks slightly different: a soft, cloudy, mottled wash across the body; noticeably lighter, abraded color along every seam line, the folded edge of the ribbed collar, the shoulder seams, the sleeve hems and the bottom hem, where the stitching shows a pale faded halo; the flat center of the chest and back keeps a deeper tone. Tiny vintage puckering along the chain-stitched seams and double-needle hems. Dry, chalky, fully matte cotton surface with zero sheen. Because the fabric is light, the wide boxy body does not stand stiffly: it collapses gently from the dropped shoulders into long relaxed vertical folds and a few soft ripples at the sides. 2x1 ribbed crew neck about 2.5 cm tall, lying flat, with a paler worn edge; shoulder-to-shoulder internal tape; the dropped shoulder seam sits well down the upper arm and also shows a faded line. Movement: fluid and airy — the loose body sways with the pose and the wide sleeves open and fall softly, with easy creases where a hand grabs the fabric.
prompt.fit: Oversized fit (size M on a 1.84 m, 84 kg man): body length 75 cm falling below the hip, chest width 59 cm — very loose and boxy, about 12 cm of ease — shoulder width 54 cm so the seam drops 4–5 cm onto the upper arm, wide sleeves 25 cm ending just above the elbow.
